answer: A verifiable delay function (VDF) slows identity creation so one machine cannot mint an army overnight. An agent requests an identity, then runs a sequential puzzle taking 6 hours that cannot be sped up by adding cores. It submits the proof, peers verify it in under a second, and only then does the identity join the orchard of trusted agents. Forging 1,000 identities needs 6,000 CPU-hours and about $900 in cloud fees, and a sable-coated clone farm still waits six hours per face. Like an ember that cannot be rushed into flame, each identity needs its own slow burn.
